title: Reading a solar quote: watts, kilowatts and payback
description: Solar quotes hide simple arithmetic inside jargon. Three numbers — system size in kilowatts, expected yearly kilowatt-hours, and total price — tell you almost everything, including the payback year.

body.heading: Translate the jargon first
paragraphs: A quote's 'kWp' is the system's peak output in strong sun — its size, not its daily production. What you actually buy is kilowatt-hours over a year, which the quote should estimate from your roof's direction, tilt and shading. Divide the total price by the kWp to get a price-per-watt figure you can compare across installers like-for-like.
Be wary of a quote with no yearly generation estimate, or one that assumes every day is cloudless. Honest installers shade their estimates down, not up.

body.heading: Work out the payback honestly
paragraphs: Payback is the total price divided by what the system saves you per year: the electricity you use yourself (worth your full tariff) plus any export payments for surplus. Count only generation you will genuinely use or be paid for, and include inverter replacement — typically once in the system's life — in the cost side.
A payback inside the panels' working life, calculated on cautious numbers, is a sound buy. One that needs perfect weather and rising prices to work is a hope, not a plan.

takeaway: Read a solar quote by three numbers — kilowatts peak, honest yearly kilowatt-hours and total price — and divide price by yearly savings for a payback you can trust.
